summary:
This bill, the “Florida Freeze Disaster Assistance Act of 2026,” makes a direct, one-time appropriation of $3.5 billion for fiscal year 2027 to the “Office of the Secretary” of the U.S. Department of Agriculture, to remain available until expended. The appropriation is drawn from the general fund of the Treasury not otherwise appropriated. The Secretary of Agriculture is directed to use the funds to provide block grants to States for losses of revenue, quality, or production of crops (including prevented planting), trees, bushes, and vines resulting from a freeze or cold weather condition. The bill expressly requires that the assistance include compensation to producers for losses of multi-year crops.

The availability of the funds is subject to three geographic and procedural provisos. First, the funds are restricted to losses occurring in counties that received a disaster designation for freeze and related cold weather conditions issued by the Secretary on March 4, 2026. Second, the funds are to be made available only upon the request of a State department of agriculture or another appropriate State agency as determined by the Secretary. Third, the Secretary must submit an implementation report to the House and Senate Committees on Appropriations not later than 120 days after enactment, and quarterly thereafter until the appropriated amounts are fully expended.

The bill contains no authorizing language separate from the appropriation; it functions as a direct emergency appropriation. The final proviso designates the entire $3.5 billion as an emergency requirement pursuant to section 251(b)(2)(A)(i) of the Balanced Budget and Emergency Deficit Control Act of 1985, thereby exempting the spending from certain budgetary enforcement mechanisms. The bill does not amend any existing statute, establish a new program outside the block grant mechanism, or impose a sunset on the authority. No matching requirements, allocation formulas, or administrative cost caps are specified.
